questions.question: Which risk came first in the OWASP Top 10 (2021 edition)?
questions.explanation: In the 2021 edition, "broken access control" came first. Injection was third, and XSS was merged into injection.

questions.question: Just by rewriting "/orders/1001" in the URL to "/orders/1002", someone else's order information can be seen. Which category is this problem closest to?
questions.explanation: The server does not check whether the logged-in user is allowed to access that data, so this is broken access control (IDOR).

questions.question: Which pair gives the threat that the "E" in STRIDE stands for and the control that mainly addresses it?
questions.explanation: The E in STRIDE is elevation of privilege, which is countered by authorization (proper access control).

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate control against the "R (Repudiation)" in STRIDE?
choices: Recording operation logs in a form that cannot be altered, and digital signatures
questions.explanation: Against someone denying "I did not do it", a trail of evidence from trustworthy logs and digital signatures is effective.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of the incident response flow set out in NIST SP 800-61 Rev. 2?
choices: Detection and analysis → preparation → post-incident activity → containment, eradication and recovery
Preparation → detection and analysis → containment, eradication and recovery → post-incident activity
Post-incident activity → preparation → detection and analysis → recovery
questions.explanation: The order is preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication and recovery, and post-incident activity (applying lessons learned). The lessons from post-incident activity feed into the next round of preparation. Note that Rev. 3, published in April 2025, was restructured around the functions of NIST CSF 2.0 (such as Detect, Respond and Recover).

questions.question: From a forensics point of view, which is the most appropriate first response to a device suspected of malware infection?
choices: Turn off the power at once and reinstall the OS
Disconnect it from the network and, if possible, preserve volatile information such as memory before investigating
Keep using it as it is and see what happens
Delete all infected files and then report
questions.explanation: The device is disconnected from the network to stop the spread, but turning off the power erases the evidence in memory, so the most volatile information is preserved first.

questions.question: Which is the correct idea behind zero trust?
choices: Access from the internal network is trusted unconditionally
Every access is verified every time, wherever it comes from, and allowed with the minimum privileges
Once connected to the VPN, a user can access every internal system
questions.explanation: Zero trust is the idea of "never trust, always verify". Each access is verified whether it comes from inside or outside.

questions.question: Which system collects logs from many kinds of devices, correlates them, and detects signs of attack?
questions.explanation: A SIEM (security information and event management) system collects and correlates logs to detect threats.

questions.question: Which knowledge base organizes attackers' tactics and techniques on the basis of real attack cases?
questions.explanation: MITRE ATT&CK organizes attackers' tactics and techniques, and is used to evaluate detection and defenses.

questions.question: What can be said when forward secrecy (PFS) is in place?
choices: Even if the server's private key leaks later, communications recorded in the past cannot be decrypted
Hash functions are no longer needed
questions.explanation: A throwaway key is created for each session with (EC)DHE or similar, so past communications stay protected even if the long-term private key leaks.

questions.question: Which mechanism makes the browser remember "always connect to this site over HTTPS" and prevents downgrades to HTTP?
questions.explanation: HSTS (HTTP Strict Transport Security) forces connections to use HTTPS and prevents downgrade attacks.

questions.question: In the cloud shared responsibility model, which of these is the customer's responsibility in every model (IaaS, PaaS and SaaS)?
choices: Physical guarding of the data center
Managing the stored data and the accounts (access rights)
questions.explanation: The physical infrastructure is the provider's responsibility, but managing data, accounts and access rights is the customer's responsibility in every model.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to generate a password reset token in Python?
choices: Use the value of time.time() as it is
questions.explanation: The random module produces predictable pseudo-random numbers and is not suitable for security purposes. Use the secrets module.

questions.question: When running an OS command in Python with a file name received from outside, which way of writing it is the safer?
questions.explanation: If the arguments are passed as a list and shell=True is not used, the input is not interpreted by the shell, which helps prevent OS command injection.

questions.question: Which is the correct pair of descriptions for CVE and CVSS?
choices: CVE = severity rating standard, CVSS = vulnerability identifier
CVE = vulnerability identifier, CVSS = severity rating standard
CVE = a vulnerability site in Japan, CVSS = an international standard
questions.explanation: CVE is a common identifier for each vulnerability, and CVSS is a standard that rates severity from 0.0 to 10.0.

questions.question: When a new serious vulnerability is announced, which of these helps you find out quickly whether your own product is affected?
questions.explanation: If an SBOM tells you which libraries and versions you use, you can check at once whether you are using the vulnerable component.

questions.question: What is the ransomware technique called in which the attackers not only encrypt data but also threaten to publish data they stole beforehand, to force payment?
questions.explanation: It is called "double extortion" because the threat has two parts: encryption and publication of information.

questions.question: Which technique publishes a malicious package with a name similar to a popular one, so that it is installed through a typing mistake?
questions.explanation: It is called typosquatting because it targets typos (typing mistakes). Check the package name and the publisher carefully.

questions.question: Which attack abuses a feature that sends requests from the server to a URL specified by the user, to reach the internal network or a cloud metadata service?
questions.explanation: SSRF (server-side request forgery) uses the server as a stepping stone to reach internal resources. It is countered by, for example, an allowlist of destinations.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to address "insecure design" in the OWASP Top 10?
choices: Only installing a WAF after release
Increasing the number of characters in passwords
Carrying out threat modeling at the design stage and building in security requirements
questions.explanation: A flaw in the design cannot be prevented even by a perfect implementation. It has to be addressed at the design stage (shift left).

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate implementation for preventing broken access control?
choices: Relying only on making IDs long numbers that are hard to guess
Verifying on the server, for each request, that the user has rights to the data in question
Checking rights with JavaScript in the browser
Preventing the action by not showing the button on screen
questions.explanation: The user can alter what is shown on screen and what runs in the browser. Rights must always be checked on the server.

questions.question: In production, a stack trace and the database structure are shown on screen when an error occurs. Which category is closest?
questions.explanation: Detailed debugging output gives attackers clues. In production, show only a general error message and record the details in the logs.

questions.question: Which pair gives the threat that the "S" in STRIDE stands for and the control that mainly addresses it?
questions.explanation: The S in STRIDE is spoofing: the threat of pretending to be another person or system. It is countered by authentication.

questions.question: Which security property does the "T (Tampering)" in STRIDE mainly violate?
questions.explanation: Tampering with data or code damages integrity. It is countered with hashes, signatures and access control.

questions.question: Which security property corresponds to the "D (Denial of service)" in STRIDE?
questions.explanation: Denial of service is a threat to availability. It is countered with redundancy, rate limiting and so on.

questions.question: What is the purpose of making "trust boundaries" clear in threat modeling?
choices: To identify where data passes between areas with different levels of trust, and to judge whether validation or authentication is needed
To count the lines of source code
To measure the speed of the network
questions.explanation: Places where data crosses a trust boundary, such as between the internet and a server, are easy to attack, so input validation and authentication matter there.

questions.question: Which is the best description of the role of a CSIRT?
choices: The department that audits the company's accounts
The department in charge of selling products
The team that receives, handles and coordinates security incidents within the organization
The team in charge of designing the website
questions.explanation: The CSIRT is the point of contact for incident response and also handles cooperation inside and outside the organization (with JPCERT/CC, for example).

questions.question: Which is an appropriate example of "containment" in incident response?
choices: Applying for a budget for a new security product
Isolating infected devices from the network and disabling compromised accounts
questions.explanation: Containment is the response that stops the damage spreading.

questions.question: In a forensic investigation, what is often used to show that an acquired disk image has not changed since it was acquired?
choices: The name of the file's author
Only a screenshot of the screen
questions.explanation: If you record the hash value at acquisition and it matches when recalculated later, you can show the image has not been altered.

questions.question: What is the purpose of recording the "chain of custody" when preserving evidence?
choices: To record who handled the evidence, when and how, and so show that the evidence is reliable
To calculate the cost of the investigation
questions.explanation: If the record of handling is broken, it can no longer be shown that the evidence was not altered, and its value as legal evidence may be lost.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate thing to do in the "post-incident activity (using lessons learned)" stage of incident response?
choices: Go back to normal work without doing anything
Make punishing the people who responded the only aim
Look back on the cause and the response, and turn them into measures to prevent recurrence and improvements to the response procedure
questions.explanation: A review that focuses on improving the system, not on assigning blame, is what matters.

questions.question: Which is the correct idea behind defense in depth?
choices: Introduce only the single strongest control
Line up many units of the same product
Layer several different controls so that if one is breached, the others can still stop the attack
questions.explanation: Controls are layered at different levels, such as the entrance, the inside, the exit, the endpoints and the data.

questions.question: Which technique divides the network into small sections and limits traffic between them to the minimum necessary, to prevent lateral movement after an intrusion?
questions.explanation: Even if an attacker gets in, the damage can be confined to one part, so it is one of the typical ways of implementing zero trust.

questions.question: Which product monitors behavior on endpoints, detects signs of compromise, and supports investigation and response?
questions.explanation: EDR (endpoint detection and response) assumes that intrusion will happen and supports detection and response.

questions.question: Which is a correct weakness of the traditional perimeter defense model?
choices: Once an attacker is inside, internal traffic is trusted, so the damage spreads easily
It cannot stop any attacks from outside at all
It can only be used with cloud services
questions.explanation: The blurring of the line between "inside" and "outside", as cloud use and remote work spread, is another reason zero trust has become widespread.

questions.question: In zero trust, which is the appropriate way to decide whether to allow an access?
choices: Allow everything if the IP address is in the same country
Decide only by whether the connection comes from the internal network
Allow forever once the user has logged in
Decide each time by combining the result of user authentication, the state of the device (such as its patch level) and the circumstances of the access
questions.explanation: Zero trust is the idea of "never trust, always verify".

questions.question: Which is an appropriate example of an IoC (indicator of compromise)?
choices: The purchase price of a server
IP addresses, domains and malware hash values used in an attack
questions.explanation: Sharing and matching IoCs lets other organizations detect the same attack too.

questions.question: What is the main role of a SOC (security operations center)?
choices: Monitoring systems and networks, and detecting, analyzing and reporting attacks
questions.explanation: The SOC handles monitoring and analysis, and works with the CSIRT when an incident occurs.

questions.question: What is the value of applying the cyber kill chain to defense?
choices: You can identify the attacker and strike back
One product can stop every attack
Logs no longer need to be kept
You can divide an attack into stages and plan controls that break the chain at an early stage
questions.explanation: Placing controls at each stage from reconnaissance to actions on objectives raises the chance of stopping the attack somewhere.

questions.question: In MITRE ATT&CK, which category corresponds to the attacker's "goal (why they take that action)"?
questions.explanation: Tactics are goals such as "initial access" and "privilege escalation". Techniques are the ways of achieving those goals.

questions.question: Which is a correct feature of TLS 1.3?
choices: Many weak ciphers were kept for compatibility with old cipher suites
It does not use symmetric-key cryptography
It does not encrypt, and only authenticates
Static RSA key exchange, which has no forward secrecy, was removed and the handshake was simplified
questions.explanation: TLS 1.3 removed static RSA key exchange, which has no forward secrecy. In normal connections that use certificates, (EC)DHE provides forward secrecy.

questions.question: Which is the correct role of ECDHE?
choices: Sharing a symmetric key safely using a temporary key for each session (key exchange)
Calculating the hash value of a file
questions.explanation: Because a throwaway key is used for each session, forward secrecy is obtained.

questions.question: What is the main reason TLS can prevent man-in-the-middle (MITM) attacks?
choices: Verifying the server certificate confirms that the other party is the legitimate server, and the content of the communication is encrypted
Because the IP address is fixed
Because the browser cache is used
questions.explanation: Certificate verification lets you tell a fake server apart. That is why it is dangerous to ignore a certificate warning and connect anyway.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT recommended as a web server setting today?
choices: Preferring key exchange methods with forward secrecy
questions.explanation: TLS 1.0 and 1.1 have known weaknesses, so they are deprecated and are disabled in the major browsers.

questions.question: What is the list of domains built into browsers in advance, so that HSTS takes effect from the very first visit, called?
questions.explanation: Normal HSTS takes effect only after one visit. A domain registered on the preload list has HTTPS enforced from the first visit.

questions.question: When using IaaS, which of these falls within the customer's responsibility?
choices: Physical entry control at the data center
Hardware maintenance of the physical servers
Applying patches to the OS on virtual machines
questions.explanation: In IaaS, everything from the OS upward (OS, middleware, applications and data) is the customer's responsibility.

questions.question: Which main responsibility stays with the customer even when using SaaS?
choices: Managing accounts and access rights, and handling the data that is stored
Applying patches to the server OS
questions.explanation: Even with SaaS, the customer manages who things are shared with and which data is put there.

questions.question: Which mechanism continuously detects cloud misconfigurations (such as storage set to public) and supports fixing them?
questions.explanation: CSPM (cloud security posture management) compares cloud settings against rules and detects problems.

questions.question: Customer data placed in cloud storage could be viewed by anyone. What is the most common cause?
choices: A power cut at the cloud provider's data center
The screen settings on the user's PC
A mistake in the access permission settings (a wrong public setting)
questions.explanation: Most cloud data leaks come from misconfiguration on the customer's side, not from a problem on the provider's side.

questions.question: Which is the appropriate way to handle a cloud root (top-level) account?
choices: Set up multi-factor authentication, do not use it for everyday work, and use individual users or roles with the minimum necessary privileges
Issue an access key and embed it in source code
Share the root account among everyone
questions.explanation: The root account can perform every operation, so the damage is enormous if it is taken over.

questions.question: Which is a dangerous way to load data received from an untrusted external source in Python?
choices: Checking it against an allowlist before using it
Validating the value and then converting it with int()
questions.explanation: pickle can run arbitrary code when loading, so it is not used for untrusted data.

questions.question: Which is the correct way to write code that prevents SQL injection with Python's sqlite3?
choices: cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '%s'" % name)
cur.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'")
questions.explanation: Use the "?" placeholder and pass the value separately. Building SQL by joining strings or with f-strings is dangerous.

questions.question: Which tool checks whether the dependency packages used in a Python project have known vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: pip-audit checks installed packages against a vulnerability database. venv is for virtual environments and black is a code formatter.

questions.question: Which tool statically analyzes Python source code and detects dangerous code such as the use of eval or shell=True in subprocess?
questions.explanation: Bandit points out code that is likely to have security problems. pytest is for testing and tkinter is a GUI library.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to handle secrets such as API keys and passwords?
choices: Do not write them in source code. Load them from environment variables or a secrets management service
Write them directly in source code and publish it with Git
questions.explanation: Once a secret has been published in Git, it is hard to remove it completely from the history. If one leaks, revoke it and issue a new one at once.

questions.question: Which is the correct description of the "KEV (Known Exploited Vulnerabilities) catalog" published by CISA?
choices: A format for a software bill of materials
A standard that rates the severity of vulnerabilities from 0 to 10
A scheme that gives an identifier to every vulnerability
A list of vulnerabilities confirmed to have been exploited, useful for prioritizing responses
questions.explanation: The identifier is CVE, the severity rating standard is CVSS, and the bill of materials is the SBOM. KEV helps you judge "whether it is actually being used in attacks".

questions.question: Which is the correct range of values for the CVSS base score?
questions.explanation: The larger the value, the more severe. For example, 9.0 or above is classed as "Critical".

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate way to think about prioritizing vulnerability responses?
choices: Consider not only the CVSS value but also real-world exploitation and the impact on your own systems (such as whether they are exposed to the internet)
Deal with them all together in the once-a-year scheduled maintenance
Deal with them in order from the oldest announcement date
Dealing with them mechanically from the highest CVSS value down is enough
questions.explanation: The CVSS base value is a general severity. Decide priority by also considering exploitation (KEV and so on) and your own environment.

questions.question: Which is the correct description of JVN?
choices: The name of an antivirus product
A portal site that provides vulnerability-related information and countermeasures for software and other products used in Japan
An international standard for rating the severity of vulnerabilities
The name of a cryptographic algorithm
questions.explanation: JVN (Japan Vulnerability Notes) is run jointly by JPCERT/CC and IPA.

questions.question: A vulnerability has been announced, but the patch cannot be applied right away. What is the appropriate response?
choices: Stop collecting logs from the system concerned
Do not share the vulnerability information within the company
Do nothing until a patch is available
Apply the workarounds the vendor gives (such as disabling a feature, restricting access, or protecting with a WAF) and plan the patching
questions.explanation: Use workarounds to make an attack harder, while monitoring the impact and planning the patching.

questions.question: Which is a correct example of a supply chain attack?
choices: Peeking at a passer-by's smartphone screen
Sending the target's server a huge number of requests to stop it
Getting into the real target company through a business partner or subsidiary with weak security
questions.explanation: Controls are needed that cover not only your own company but also business partners and software suppliers.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate defense against software supply chain attacks?
choices: Treat a package as the same one if the name is similar, and install it
Pin the versions of dependency packages, verify hash values and signatures, and keep track of the makeup with an SBOM
Give every developer administrator privileges on production
Always update dependency packages automatically to the latest version without checking them
questions.explanation: Knowing and verifying what you take in, and from where, is the basis of supply chain security.

questions.question: Which route of intrusion has been reported especially often in recent ransomware damage in Japan?
choices: Exploiting vulnerabilities or credentials of VPN devices and Remote Desktop
A fax sent to the wrong number
questions.explanation: In the National Police Agency's reports, intrusions through VPN devices and Remote Desktop account for most cases. Fixing vulnerabilities in internet-facing devices and using multi-factor authentication are important.

questions.question: Which is the most appropriate preparation against ransomware damage?
choices: Just take out insurance, because paying the ransom always restores everything
Delete all the logs if infected
Keep backups only in a shared folder on the same network
Prepare offline or immutable (unchangeable) backups and practice the recovery procedure
questions.explanation: Attackers go after backups too, encrypting or deleting them. Paying does not guarantee recovery or deletion of the stolen data.

questions.question: Which is correct about IPA's "10 Major Security Threats"?
choices: It covers only threats to individuals
It is a ranking of antivirus software
IPA selects and publishes it every year, based on incidents and other events of the previous year
The International Organization for Standardization publishes it every 10 years
questions.explanation: Threats are selected from two viewpoints, "individuals" and "organizations". Check the latest edition to see which threats are getting attention now.

questions.question: Which correctly describes the relationship between OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect?
choices: OAuth 2.0 is a framework for authorization, and OpenID Connect adds authentication with an ID token on top of it
OAuth 2.0 handles authentication and OpenID Connect handles authorization
OpenID Connect is an old version of OAuth 2.0
questions.explanation: OAuth 2.0 is an authorization mechanism that grants access to APIs. For authentication, that is, checking who the user is, you use OpenID Connect, which issues an ID token.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using PKCE in the authorization code flow?
choices: To make the user's password longer
To remove the expiry of tokens
To stop an attacker from exchanging an intercepted authorization code for tokens
questions.explanation: With PKCE, a value known only to the app that started the authorization request is checked when the code is exchanged for tokens. A stolen authorization code cannot be exchanged.

questions.question: Which is the right way to validate a JWT you receive?
choices: Verify the signature, issuer (iss), audience (aud) and expiry (exp), and fix the algorithm on the receiving side
Read and use the contents without verifying the signature
Use whatever algorithm is written in the token's header, unconditionally
Accept it even if it has expired
questions.explanation: If you skip verification or leave the algorithm up to the token, you end up accepting forged tokens (attacks such as alg=none).

questions.question: What is the main reason containers are said to be less isolated than virtual machines?
choices: They always run with root privileges
They share the host's OS kernel
questions.explanation: Containers share the host's kernel. A kernel vulnerability or a dangerous setting can let an attacker break out to the host.

questions.question: Which is an appropriate runtime setting for a container?
choices: Always run in privileged mode because it is convenient
Run as a non-root user and do not use privileged mode
questions.explanation: Keeping privileges narrow limits the impact on the host and other containers even if the app in the container is compromised.

questions.question: In Kubernetes, which mechanism limits communication between Pods to only what is needed?
questions.explanation: Limiting traffic with network policies makes it easier to stop lateral movement to other Pods even if one Pod is compromised.
